note: Shipped ABI profiles, transcribed from docs/analysis.md §4.6. calibrate.mjs uses these
ONLY as a cross-check (assertion (d)). The calibrator under test must never be given
them: a driver that reports `usedProfile: true` fails the run outright, because the
whole point of §8.9 is evidence that the calibrator solves layouts it has never seen.
Provenance matters for reading a mismatch. The §4.6 numbers were recovered by
disassembling untapped-scry and then live-validated (30/30 in §12.3, 21/21 in §12.3b,
60/60 in §12.4c) against Slay the Spire 2 — which runs a MODIFIED 4.5.1 engine. A stock
4.5.1 export template is not the same binary. So a disagreement on the
4.5.1-release-single cell has two readings, and the harness prints both rather than
picking one: (a) the calibrator is wrong, or (b) the stock template's Control layout
differs from the StS2 fork's. Only (a) blocks publishing.

comment: control.anchor is not read by scry; it is included because §4.6's cross-check against
upstream scene/gui/control.h places Data.anchor[4] immediately after Data.offset[4],
and a calibrator that mistakes anchor for offset would otherwise look correct on the
nodes whose anchors are all zero. Main.tscn's AnchoredWide exists to break that tie.

profiles.verifiedAgainst: stock 4.5 debug export templates, grid series 2026-08-17 (3 passes × 2 bindings, zero cross-run disagreement)
supersededTable: This column was REPLACED on 2026-08-17 with the grid's measurement. It previously held
scry's disassembled debug constants (node.parent 0x178, visible 0x3c0, label.text 0x848,
richTextLabel.text 0xb18, ...), which the grid contradicted 8 of 13 times across three
passes on unchanged stock binaries. Those constants were also self-inconsistent: getOffset
read 0x500..0x50c while getPosition read 0x508/0x50c, and control.scale (0x4f8) sat BELOW
control.offset (0x500), inverting the field order that the release column and upstream
control.h both agree on. §8.9 asked for the debug column to be measured; it now is.
The measured rule is uniform: DEBUG = RELEASE + 8, every field, no exceptions. Confirmed
on 4.5 and independently on 4.3 (§12.7), and corroborated a third way by the getter
decoder (§13.6), which finds no getter loading the old 0x848 anywhere in the 4.5 debug
template while its structural twin loads 0x808.
scriptInstance.ownerBackref is now a per-CLASS map, and the class is the implementing C++
ScriptInstance type read off the instance's own vtable by RTTI — NOT the cell's binding.
That distinction is load-bearing and was nearly encoded wrong: CSharpInstance and
GDScriptInstance are unrelated classes implementing one interface, and a mono export
template runs .gd scripts perfectly well, so a SINGLE PROCESS can hold nodes of both kinds
at once. The correct value therefore differs per NODE, not per build. This grid only makes
it look build-shaped because each cell's probe script happens to match its cell name.
Measured 0x8 / 0x10 across 19 of 24 cell-runs with zero contradictions.
checks.mjs accepts either shape per key: a scalar compares as before, an object resolves
against derivation.walk.scriptInstanceClass. A key this table cannot express for a given
target is NOT COMPARED rather than scored — and says so in the detail line, so the table
never reads as more complete than it is.
